newsitem.title: UK: Dollar recovers steam, targets hold above 116 yen.
newsitem.headline: Dollar recovers steam, targets hold above 116 yen.

text.p: The dollar charged higher to stand near 116 yen in early Europe, and over two yen up from late Wednesday, as Japanese and U.S. officials continued to will the U.S. unit higher.
"The comments by the Japanese that the yen has gone too far and too fast and rates are not going up are finally filtering through," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.
The Japanese government has been battling to give the dollar a leg-up after the unit sank to five-month lows of 111.88 yen on Tuesday on expectations that Japan may soon raise interest rates.

At 0800 GMT dollar/yen was trading at 115.85/5.95 vs 113.60/70 in late Europe on Wednesday. Dollar/mark was a touch firmer in early Europe and stood at 1.6985/90 against 1.6916/21 marks in late Europe on Wednesday

"Certainly, Japanese policy makers appear keen to inject a note of calm into the market, and speculation about an imminent rate hike from the BoJ (Bank of Japan) also appear to be abating," said Paul Meggyesi, currency strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Analysts said the U.S. unit also appeared well bid after finding a floor below 112 yen earlier this week.
"The comments have become a bit more urgent," said Ferridge.

In the latest round of verbal intervention, Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) said it agrees with the BOJ's low interest-rate policy and that concerns about excessive yen weakness are now completely gone.
Earlier, Takashini Anzai, executive director of the BoJ, said: "correction to the yen's excessive weakness has begun, but the pace has been too rapid."
Some support for the ailing dollar was also received after U.S. Trade Secretary Robert Rubin reiterated the U.S.'s strong-dollar policy.
Against the mark, the dollar gained some ground after German April M3 growth slowed to annualised 6.7 percent against fourth-quarter 1996 from 8.3 percent in March and a 7.7 percent forecast.
But by 0850 GMT, it had eased off its highs and stood at 1.6955/65 against earlier peaks just above 1.7000 marks.
